  366: \smallskip
  367: \noindent\textbf{Relation to density and approximation literature.} For ordinary
  368: automatic sets, asymptotic density questions go back at least to
  369: Berstel \cite{Berstel1973}; the standard global sources include
  370: B\"uchi's automata-theoretic decidability work \cite{Buchi1960} and
  371: Allouche--Shallit's monograph on automatic sequences
  372: \cite{AlloucheShallit2003}. Matrix and algorithmic treatments appear
  373: in
  374: \cite{BodirskyGaertnerVonOertzenSchwinghammer2004,Bell2020UpperDensity},
  375: and Koga's paper \cite{Koga2019Density} revisits Sin'ya's density-zero
  376: criterion \cite{Sinya2021}. The rational-measure viewpoint of Hansel
  377: and Perrin \cite{HanselPerrin1989} interprets regular languages via
  378: probability measures on shifts of finite type. Kozik's MFCS 2005 paper
  379: \cite{Kozik2005Conditional} formulates conditional densities for
  380: deterministic presentations in the trim strongly connected setting,
  381: Montoya \cite{Montoya2025Relative} recasts these questions in terms of
  382: relative densities, and Berth\'e--Goulet-Ouellet--Perrin
  383: \cite{BertheGouletPerrin2025} establish a broad density theorem under
  384: shift-invariant measures. Accordingly,
  385: \suppref{Theorem~1.2}, \Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-powerlaw}, and
  386: \suppref{Theorem~1.18}
  387: should be read here as background statements in a form suited to the
  388: prime-slice applications, while
  389: \suppref{Theorem~1.14} is the exponent-sensitive
  390: extension needed for general trim deterministic presentations. Cobham's
  391: theorem
  392: \cite{Cobham1969} is the foundational reference for base-dependent
  393: automatic recognizability of sets of integers. Regular approximation of
  394: non-regular languages is a separate line of work; see, for example,
  395: Eisman and Ravikumar \cite{EismanRavikumar2005} and the asymptotic
  396: approximation framework of Sin'ya \cite{Sinya2021}. Polynomial and
  397: sparse growth phenomena for regular languages are part of the classical
  398: transfer-matrix picture \cite{Berstel1973,SalomaaSoittola1978}, and
  399: numeration systems on regular languages are treated in
  400: \cite{LecomteRigo2001,Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,CharlierRampersad2011,Rigo2014Vol1,Rigo2014Vol2}.
  401: The present contribution is narrower: it packages the fixed-DFA
  402: prime-slice obstruction with computable residue-class constants and
  403: explicit thresholds, then applies the same finite-budget argument in the
  404: Zeckendorf setting.
  405:

  407: \medskip
  408: \noindent\textbf{Summary.} \suppref{Theorem~1.2 and Lemma~1.16} and
  409: \Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-powerlaw}
  410: record the density statements needed for deterministic presentations.
  411: \suppref{Theorem~1.14} gives the general trim
  412: deterministic finite-budget theorem, including multiple maximal
  413: components, Perron-active residue classes, and their polynomial factors,
  414: and \suppref{Theorem~1.18} records the strongly connected
  415: specialization used for Zeckendorf. The paper's effective contribution
  416: is the finite-budget obstruction mechanism with quantitative fixed-DFA
  417: recall/precision and symmetric-difference instances; see
  418: \suppref{Corollary~1.19}, \suppref{Proposition~1.9},
  419: \suppref{Corollary~1.10}, and \suppref{Corollary~1.12}.
  420: The Zeckendorf analogues are
  421: \Cref{cor:zeck-symmetric-diff,cor:zeck-recall-precision}. The
  422: Zeckendorf prime-language theorem is downstream of the PNT-free
  423: coprime-quotient pumping theorem
  424: \Cref{thm:coprime-quotient-zeckendorf-pumping}. Its principal
  425: consequences are
  426: \Cref{cor:unbounded-distinct-prime-divisors,cor:bounded-distinct-prime-zeckendorf-languages-reg-immune}
  427: and \Cref{cor:finite-prime-support-zeckendorf-languages-reg-immune};
  428: \Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-slice-rigidity} remains a separate
  429: slice-cardinality obstruction, and
  430: \Cref{cor:zeckendorf-prime-language-not-regular} is an immediate
  431: consequence of REG-immunity.
  432: Context-free Zeckendorf pumping is
  433: \Cref{thm:context-free-coprime-quotient-zeckendorf-pumping}, with the
  434: immunity consequences in
  435: \Cref{cor:zeckendorf-context-free-immunity-package}. The stronger MCFL
  436: package is
  437: \Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit,thm:mcfl-local-adic-fingerprint,prop:local-prime-factor-cb-rank,thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy,thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray,cor:bounded-outside-support-semidecidable,thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain,thm:unit-mcfl-divisibility-tree};
  438: its linear Pisot specialization is
  439: \Cref{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity,cor:linear-pisot-prime-cf-immunity}.
  440: The eventual-sofic exclusion is recorded only as the brief consequence
  441: \Cref{rem:zeckendorf-primes-not-sofic}, while
  442: \suppref{Theorem~A.1} and \suppref{Proposition~A.2}
  443: remain classical background.
  444: 
  445: \medskip
  446: Finite-automata non-recognizability of the base-\(b\) prime language
  447: goes back to Minsky and Papert \cite{MinskyPapert1966}.
  448: Allen \cite{Allen1968}, Hartmanis--Shank
  449: \cite{HartmanisShank1968}, and Sch\"utzenberger
  450: \cite{Schutzenberger1968} proved stronger related results for broader
  451: language classes and acceptable sets. Shallit's survey and monograph
  452: treat automaticity and number theory from the finite-automata viewpoint
  453: \cite{Shallit1996,AlloucheShallit2003}. Recent work of Yuen and Dubbe
  454: studies regularity and quantitative automaticity around the prime set
  455: \cite{Yuen2022,Dubbe2024}, and Shen proves that prime automata in Yao's
  456: finite-automata primeness model do not exist \cite{Shen2022}. Those
  457: results concern
  458: recognizability or growing-state quantitative automaticity. The present
  459: theorems are different: the automaton is fixed, the comparison is made
  460: on each fixed length slice, and the conclusion is a recall/precision
  461: or symmetric-difference obstruction rather than a state lower bound for
  462: a sequence of automata.
  463: 
  464: The Zeckendorf theorem in \Cref{sec:zeckendorf} should be compared with,
  465: but not identified with, the classical base-representation results of
  466: Sch\"utzenberger. In a fixed base the digit value update is controlled
  467: by multiplication by the base modulo a prime. For LSD-first Zeckendorf
  468: words the corresponding update is instead the unimodular \(3\times3\)
  469: matrix action on
  470: \((\val(\text{prefix}),F_{r+1},F_{r+2})^t\). This invertibility modulo
  471: the square of the current value is what makes the pumping congruence
  472: work and yields quotients \(Q_i\equiv1\pmod {N_i}\). Thus the quotient
  473: is coprime to the previous value, forcing new rational prime divisors;
  474: the prime-language REG-immunity is the \(K=1\) bounded-distinct-prime
  475: subcase.
  476: 
  477: The interaction between primes and digital
  478: constraints has a much deeper literature. Mauduit and Rivat
  479: \cite{MauduitRivat2010}, Drmota--Mauduit--Rivat
  480: \cite{DrmotaMauduitRivat2009}, and M\"ullner \cite{Muellner2017} prove
  481: analytic equidistribution results for digit functions and automatic
  482: sequences evaluated at primes. Maynard's theorem on primes with missing
  483: digits \cite{Maynard2019}, Bourgain's work on primes with prescribed
  484: binary digits
  485: \cite{Bourgain2013PrescribedDigits,Bourgain2015PrescribedDigitsII},
  486: Swaenepoel's extension to a positive proportion of preassigned digits
  487: in arbitrary bases \cite{Swaenepoel2020PreassignedDigits}, and
  488: Bhowmik--Suzuki's work on reversed primes in arithmetic progressions
  489: \cite{BhowmikSuzuki2024} address complementary problems about primes
  490: and digital restrictions. These analytic results allow the digit
  491: constraints to vary with the length and prove prime
  492: asymptotics or positive proportions inside those varying families. The
  493: present paper does neither: the automaton is fixed once and for all,
  494: and the obstruction is the elementary mismatch between eventual
  495: periodic finite-state densities and the finite prime budget
  496: \(\asymp\lambda^m/m\). For Zeckendorf and more general Parry numeration
  497: systems, the uniqueness theorem goes back to Lekkerkerker and
  498: Zeckendorf \cite{Lekkerkerker1952,Zeckendorf1972}, and the regularity
  499: of admissible expansions is standard; see
  500: \cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Rigo2014Vol1,Rigo2014Vol2}. Analytic
  501: work of Drmota--M\"ullner--Spiegelhofer on primes in Fibonacci or
  502: Zeckendorf representations \cite{DrmotaMuellnerSpiegelhofer2021}
  503: studies prime distribution under numeration constraints. Here we use
  504: only the size of the Zeckendorf interval and regular syntax, not an
  505: equidistribution theorem for Zeckendorf digit patterns. The
  506: transfer-matrix viewpoint on word counts is familiar from symbolic
  507: dynamics and analytic combinatorics
  508: \cite{LindMarcus1995,Kitchens1998,FlajoletSedgewick2009}.
  509: 
  510: Recent Monatshefte work illustrates the surrounding symbolic-dynamical
  511: landscape: Bustos-Gajardo--Kellendonk--Yassawi use finite semigroup
  512: methods for factors of substitution shifts
  513: \cite{BustosKellendonkYassawi2025}, and Charlier--Cisternino study
  514: soficity phenomena in Cantor real-base expansions
  515: \cite{CharlierCisternino2021}. These are complementary to the present
  516: finite-budget obstruction; they do not supply, and are not used as, a
  517: prime-slice density theorem.
  518: 
  519: For clarity, the comparison with prior work can be summarized as follows.
  520: Regular-language density results of
  521: \cite{HanselPerrin1989,Kozik2005Conditional,Koga2019Density,Montoya2025Relative,BertheGouletPerrin2025}
  522: give the periodic or conditional density statements used here; the new
  523: increment is to feed the resulting residue constants into explicit
  524: prime-slice thresholds for one fixed automaton. Numeration-system work
  525: \cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,CharlierRampersad2011,Rigo2014Vol1,Rigo2014Vol2}
  526: supplies regular admissible languages and growth laws for abstract
  527: numeration, including Zeckendorf-type systems; in the trim strongly
  528: connected cases stated explicitly, the present paper transfers the same
  529: fixed-prime-slice obstruction to Zeckendorf length slices with computable
  530: constants. For primes in Fibonacci or Zeckendorf representations, we use
  531: only the prime number theorem estimate
  532: \(\#\{p\in[F_{m+1},F_{m+2})\}\asymp\varphi^m/m\), and no distribution
  533: theorem for Zeckendorf digit patterns is claimed.
  534: 
  535: The sofic and orbit-growth papers
  536: \cite{BustosKellendonkYassawi2025,CharlierCisternino2021}, together with
  537: the classical zeta references recalled in \suppref{Appendix~A}, are used
  538: only for contextual comparison: the present argument separates those
  539: phenomena from the fixed prime-slice density obstruction. Similarly,
  540: regular-approximation frameworks for nonregular languages
  541: \cite{EismanRavikumar2005,Sinya2021} position the problem, but the
  542: obstruction proved here is slice-wise and quantitative for one fixed DFA,
  543: not an optimal approximation scheme. The main theorem chain,
  544: \suppref{Theorem~1.7}, \suppref{Theorem~1.14}, and
  545: \suppref{Corollary~1.19},
  546: computes residue alternatives, thresholds, and constants for a fixed
  547: finite automaton, and compares multicomponent polynomial exponents
  548: against a prime budget of order \(\lambda^m/m\).
  549: 
  550: \subsection{Organisation}
  551: 
  552: \suppref{Section~1} proves the density dichotomy for deterministic
  553: automata and derives the fixed-base prime corollaries.
  554: \Cref{sec:zeckendorf} records the background growth law for regular
  555: Zeckendorf sublanguages, deduces the corresponding quantitative prime
  556: corollaries, proves the PNT-free coprime-quotient Zeckendorf pumping
  557: theorem and its unbounded-\(\omega\), bounded-distinct-prime,
  558: finite-prime-support, and prime-language REG-immunity corollaries,
  559: records the older slice-level
  560: rigidity as a separate density obstruction, and then notes the easy
  561: nonregularity and sofic exclusions.
  562: \Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} proves the paired-pump Zeckendorf theorem,
  563: the synchronized MCFL orbit, its local-adic and Cantor--Bendixson
  564: consequences, the nonunit escape dichotomy, the geometric-ray
  565: characterization and its positive semidecidability consequence, and the
  566: unit-system divisibility tree, then specializes the recurrent interface
  567: to linear Pisot \(U\)-systems.
  568: \suppref{Appendix~A} collects final background analytic comparators
  569: concerning Euler products and scalar determinant models. Later sections
  570: cite the statements recorded above directly, so their proofs and
  571: corollaries need not restate the results in full.

 1301:   \(\delta_N(q,a)=q'\) for some \(a\in\Sigma\) is strongly connected.
 1302: 
 1303:   If \(\mathcal A=(Q_A,\Sigma,\delta_A,q_A,F_A)\) is another
 1304:   deterministic automaton over the same alphabet, its synchronous
 1305:   product with \(\mathcal N\) has state set \(Q_N\times Q_A\), initial
 1306:   state \((q_N,q_A)\), accepting set \(F_N\times F_A\), and the partial
 1307:   transition
 1308:   \[
 1309:     (q,s)\xrightarrow{a}(\delta_N(q,a),\delta_A(s,a))
 1310:   \]
 1311:   exactly for letters \(a\) for which both displayed transitions are
 1312:   defined. Completing \(\mathcal A\) by a sink state, when desired, does
 1313:   not change the intersection language.
 1314: \end{definition}

 1316: We first record the finite-budget statement in the general
 1317: multicomponent form. This is the version needed when the deterministic
 1318: presentation is trim but its adjacency matrix has several maximal
 1319: strongly connected components, possibly connected by transient paths.
 1320: The polynomial factors in the statement are exactly the factors absent
 1321: from the strongly connected specialization below.
 1322: 
 1323: \noindent\textit{\(\lambda\)-active residues.}
 1324: Let \(\mathcal N\) be a trim deterministic presentation with adjacency
 1325: matrix \(B_N\), let \(\lambda=\rho(B_N)>1\), and let
 1326: \(z_m=\abs{L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m}\). After a period \(D\) has been
 1327: fixed, call a residue class \(r\bmod D\) \(\lambda\)-active if
 1328: \[
 1329:   z_m\not=O(\theta^m)
 1330:   \qquad (m\equiv r\pmod D)
 1331: \]
 1332: for every \(\theta<\lambda\). Equivalently, accepted words in that
 1333: residue class have exponential growth rate \(\lambda\). A residue class
 1334: can contain infinitely many accepted lengths without being
 1335: \(\lambda\)-active: in a reducible presentation those words may be
 1336: supplied only by components of smaller spectral radius. The
 1337: multicomponent theorem below separates this lower-growth phenomenon
 1338: from the Perron-scale comparison.
 1339: 
 1340: \begin{theorem}[Multicomponent finite-budget obstruction]
 1341:   \label{thm:multicomponent-finite-budget}
 1342:   Let \(\mathcal N\) be a trim deterministic presentation,
 1343:   not necessarily strongly connected, with adjacency matrix \(B_N\).
 1344:   Let \(\lambda:=\rho(B_N)>1\), and put
 1345:   \(z_m=\abs{L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m}\). Then there are an integer
 1346:   period \(D\ge1\), a number \(0<\theta<\lambda\), an integer
 1347:   \(S\ge0\), and, for every residue \(r\bmod D\), an exponent
 1348:   \(s_r\in\{-\infty,0,\dots,S\}\) and a constant \(d_r\ge0\) such that
 1349:   \(s_r\ge0\) and \(d_r>0\) exactly on the \(\lambda\)-active residue
 1350:   classes, while \(s_r=-\infty\) and \(d_r=0\) on all other residue
 1351:   classes. On every residue class
 1352:   \[
 1353:     z_m
 1354:     =
 1355:     \lambda^m
 1356:     \left(
 1357:       d_r m^{s_r}
 1358:       +O(m^{s_r-1})
 1359:     \right)
 1360:     +O(\theta^m m^S),
 1361:     \qquad m\equiv r\pmod D .
 1362:   \]
 1363:   The convention is that the \(O(m^{-1})\) term is absent when
 1364:   \(s_r=0\), and the displayed polynomial part is absent when
 1365:   \(s_r=-\infty\). Thus non-\(\lambda\)-active residue classes, even
 1366:   those with infinitely many accepted lengths, are absorbed into the
 1367:   sub-Perron error term.
 1368: 
 1369:   For every deterministic automaton \(\mathcal A\) over \(\Sigma\) and
 1370:   \[
 1371:     a_m(\mathcal A,\mathcal N)
 1372:     :=\abs{L(\mathcal A)\cap L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m},
 1373:   \]
 1374:   after replacing \(D,S,\theta\) by common choices, there are
 1375:   constants \(e_r\ge0\) and exponents
 1376:   \(t_r\in\{-\infty,0,\dots,S\}\) such that on every residue class
 1377:   \[
 1378:     a_m(\mathcal A,\mathcal N)
 1379:     =
 1380:     \lambda^m
 1381:     \left(
 1382:       e_r m^{t_r}
 1383:       +O(m^{t_r-1})
 1384:     \right)
 1385:     +O(\theta^m m^S),
 1386:   \]
 1387:   with the same convention when \(t_r=0\); if the intersection has
 1388:   exponential growth \(<\lambda\) on that residue, then \(t_r=-\infty\)
 1389:   and the first displayed polynomial part is absent. Moreover, whenever
 1390:   \(r\bmod D\) is \(\lambda\)-active, either \(t_r=-\infty\) or
 1391:   \(t_r\le s_r\), and if \(t_r=s_r\) then \(0\le e_r\le d_r\).
 1392: 
 1393:   Consequently, let \(T_m\subseteq L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m\) satisfy
 1394:   \[
 1395:     \alpha\frac{\lambda^m}{m}
 1396:     \le \abs{T_m}
 1397:     \le \beta\frac{\lambda^m}{m}
 1398:   \]
 1399:   for all sufficiently large \(m\) in every \(\lambda\)-active residue
 1400:   class, with fixed \(\alpha,\beta>0\). For every fixed deterministic automaton
 1401:   \(\mathcal A\) there is a constant
 1402:   \(C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal N,T}>0\) such that
 1403:   \[
 1404:     \abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m)\triangle T_m}
 1405:     \ge
 1406:     C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal N,T}\frac{\lambda^m}{m}
 1407:   \]
 1408:   for all sufficiently large \(m\) in \(\lambda\)-active residue
 1409:   classes. On each \(\lambda\)-active residue class either the recall
 1410:   against \(T_m\) tends to \(0\) exponentially or polynomially, or else
 1411:   the precision is \(O(1/m)\) whenever it is defined.
 1412: \end{theorem}
 1413: 
 1414: \begin{proof}
 1415:   Put \(B_N\) in Frobenius normal form. For a finite non-negative
 1416:   integer matrix, the rational generating function
 1417:   \(u_N^{\mathsf T}(I-xB_N)^{-1}v_N\) has poles at reciprocals of
 1418:   eigenvalues of \(B_N\), and the coefficients are finite sums of
 1419:   terms \(p_{\mu}(m)\mu^m\), where \(p_\mu\) is a polynomial whose
 1420:   degree is one less than the size of the largest Jordan block attached
 1421:   to \(\mu\), plus exponentially smaller terms. Equivalently, this is
 1422:   the Frobenius normal form or transfer-matrix expansion for regular
 1423:   languages; see \cite{SalomaaSoittola1978,BerstelReutenauer2011}.
 1424:   For a non-negative matrix, the eigenvalues of modulus \(\lambda\)
 1425:   that contribute to accepted paths are roots of unity times
 1426:   \(\lambda\), arising from maximal components and chains between them.
 1427:   Taking \(D\) to be a common period of those components makes the
 1428:   peripheral factors constant on each residue class. On a fixed residue
 1429:   \(r\bmod D\), look only at the terms whose exponential factor has
 1430:   modulus \(\lambda\). If no such term contributes to accepted paths in
 1431:   that residue, then the whole residue-class count has exponential
 1432:   growth \(<\lambda\); after enlarging \(\theta\) below \(\lambda\), it
 1433:   is included in \(O(\theta^m m^S)\), and we set \(s_r=-\infty\) and
 1434:   \(d_r=0\). This case includes residues with infinitely many accepted
 1435:   lengths supplied only by smaller components.
 1436: 
 1437:   If a Perron-scale term does contribute, collect the largest remaining
 1438:   polynomial degree as \(s_r\). The leading coefficient \(d_r\) is the
 1439:   sum of the non-negative leading contributions of maximal
 1440:   component-chains realizing that residue at that degree. This sum is
 1441:   positive, because at least one such Perron-scale chain contributes
 1442:   and no cancellation is possible for counts of paths in a
 1443:   non-negative matrix. These are precisely the \(\lambda\)-active
 1444:   residues, and the displayed expansion for \(z_m\) follows.
 1445: 
 1446:   Form the synchronous product of \(\mathcal N\) with \(\mathcal A\),
 1447:   trim unreachable or non-coaccessible states, and let \(B'\) be its
 1448:   adjacency matrix. Its accepted-word count is
 1449:   \(a_m(\mathcal A,\mathcal N)=u'^{\mathsf T}(B')^m v'\), so the same
 1450:   transfer-matrix expansion applies. Its exponential growth rate is at
 1451:   most \(\lambda\), because every accepted product word projects
 1452:   injectively to a word of \(L(\mathcal N)\). If the product growth rate
 1453:   is \(<\lambda\) on a residue class, it is absorbed into
 1454:   \(O(\theta^m m^S)\) after increasing \(\theta\) below \(\lambda\) and
 1455:   increasing \(S\). If the product has growth \(\lambda\), its leading
 1456:   polynomial degree on a \(\lambda\)-active residue cannot exceed \(s_r\);
 1457:   otherwise \(a_m(\mathcal A,\mathcal N)\le z_m\) would fail along that
 1458:   residue for large \(m\). The same inequality gives \(e_r\le d_r\)
 1459:   when \(t_r=s_r\).
 1460: 
 1461:   Fix a \(\lambda\)-active residue class and put
 1462:   \(A_m=L(\mathcal A)\cap L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m\). If
 1463:   \(t_r=-\infty\), then \(\abs{A_m}=O(\theta^m m^S)\), and hence
 1464:   \[
 1465:     \frac{\abs{A_m\cap T_m}}{\abs{T_m}}
 1466:     \le
 1467:     O(m^{S+1}(\theta/\lambda)^m),
 1468:   \]
 1469:   so recall decays exponentially and
 1470:   \(\abs{A_m\triangle T_m}\ge(\alpha/2)\lambda^m/m\) for all large
 1471:   \(m\) in the residue.
 1472: 
 1473:   Suppose next that the first non-zero leading term in the expansion of
 1474:   \(a_m(\mathcal A,\mathcal N)\) on this residue is
 1475:   \(\gamma_r\lambda^m m^{u_r}\), with \(\gamma_r>0\) and \(u_r\ge0\).
 1476:   Then, for all large \(m\) in the residue,
 1477:   \(\abs{A_m}\ge(\gamma_r/2)\lambda^m m^{u_r}\). Since
 1478:   \(\abs{T_m}\le\beta\lambda^m/m\),
 1479:   \[
 1480:     \abs{A_m\triangle T_m}
 1481:     \ge \abs{A_m}-\abs{T_m}
 1482:     \ge \frac{\gamma_r}{4}\lambda^m m^{u_r}
 1483:     \ge \frac{\gamma_r}{4}\frac{\lambda^m}{m},
 1484:   \]
 1485:   after enlarging the threshold. Whenever \(\abs{A_m}>0\),
 1486:   \[
 1487:     \frac{\abs{A_m\cap T_m}}{\abs{A_m}}
 1488:     \le
 1489:     \frac{2\beta}{\gamma_r}\frac{1}{m^{u_r+1}}
 1490:     \le
 1491:     \frac{2\beta}{\gamma_r}\frac1m .
 1492:   \]
 1493:   If no such non-zero polynomial term exists, the residue is in the
 1494:   exponentially smaller case already handled. There are only finitely
 1495:   many \(\lambda\)-active residue classes, so taking the minimum of the
 1496:   positive constants obtained above proves the uniform finite-budget
 1497:   bound. The theorem makes no prime-scale conclusion on
 1498:   non-\(\lambda\)-active residues, where \(L(\mathcal N)\) itself has
 1499:   sub-Perron growth and a target of size \(\asymp\lambda^m/m\) cannot
 1500:   be a subset of \(L(\mathcal N)\cap\Sigma^m\) for all large \(m\).
 1501: \end{proof}

 1506: \(\mathcal N\) is the canonical presentation of a regular numeration
 1507: system. Write
 1508: \[

 1514: \(\lambda:=\rho(B_N)>1\) be its spectral radius, and let \(d_N\ge 1\)
 1515: be the period of \(B_N\).
 1516: 
 1517: \begin{lemma}[Cyclic-class path threshold]

   72: def identity(size: int) -> Matrix:
   73:     return tuple(
   74:         tuple(1 if row == column else 0 for column in range(size))
   75:         for row in range(size)
   76:     )

   79: def matmul(left: Matrix, right: Matrix, modulus: int | None = None) -> Matrix:
   80:     rows = len(left)
   81:     inner = len(right)
   82:     columns = len(right[0])
   83:     entries = []
   84:     for row in range(rows):
   85:         out_row = []
   86:         for column in range(columns):
   87:             value = sum(left[row][k] * right[k][column] for k in range(inner))
   88:             out_row.append(value if modulus is None else value % modulus)
   89:         entries.append(tuple(out_row))
   90:     return tuple(entries)
   91: 
   92: 
   93: def matvec(matrix: Matrix, vector: Sequence[int]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
   94:     return tuple(
   95:         sum(matrix[row][column] * vector[column] for column in range(len(vector)))
   96:         for row in range(len(matrix))
   97:     )

  100: def determinant(matrix: Matrix) -> int:
  101:     size = len(matrix)
  102:     if size == 1:
  103:         return matrix[0][0]
  104:     total = 0
  105:     for column, entry in enumerate(matrix[0]):
  106:         minor = tuple(
  107:             tuple(row[j] for j in range(size) if j != column)
  108:             for row in matrix[1:]
  109:         )
  110:         total += (-1) ** column * entry * determinant(minor)
  111:     return total
  112: 
  113: 
  114: def digit_matrix(system: LinearSystem, digit: int) -> Matrix:
  115:     if not 0 <= digit <= system.max_digit:
  116:         raise ValueError(f"digit {digit} is outside {system.name}'s alphabet")
  117:     d = system.dimension
  118:     rows = [[0] * (d + 1) for _ in range(d + 1)]
  119:     rows[0][0] = 1
  120:     rows[0][1] = digit
  121:     for index in range(d - 1):
  122:         rows[index + 1][index + 2] = 1
  123:     for index, coefficient in enumerate(system.recurrence):
  124:         rows[d][index + 1] = coefficient
  125:     return tuple(tuple(row) for row in rows)
  126:

  128: def block_matrix(system: LinearSystem, word: Sequence[int]) -> Matrix:
  129:     matrix = identity(system.dimension + 1)
  130:     for digit in word:
  131:         matrix = matmul(digit_matrix(system, digit), matrix)
  132:     return matrix

  135: def weights(system: LinearSystem, count: int) -> list[int]:
  136:     values = list(system.initials)
  137:     while len(values) < count:
  138:         values.append(
  139:             sum(
  140:                 coefficient * values[-system.dimension + index]
  141:                 for index, coefficient in enumerate(system.recurrence)
  142:             )
  143:         )
  144:     return values[:count]

  147: def value(system: LinearSystem, word: Sequence[int]) -> int:
  148:     return sum(digit * weight for digit, weight in zip(word, weights(system, len(word))))

  151: def greedy_word(system: LinearSystem, number: int) -> Word:
  152:     if number <= 0:
  153:         return ()
  154:     available = list(system.initials)
  155:     while available[-1] <= number:
  156:         available.append(
  157:             sum(
  158:                 coefficient * available[-system.dimension + index]
  159:                 for index, coefficient in enumerate(system.recurrence)
  160:             )
  161:         )
  162:     if available[-1] > number:
  163:         available.pop()
  164:     digits_msd = []
  165:     remainder = number
  166:     for weight in reversed(available):
  167:         digit, remainder = divmod(remainder, weight)
  168:         if digit > system.max_digit:
  169:             raise ValueError(f"digit bound too small for {system.name}")
  170:         digits_msd.append(digit)
  171:     if remainder:
  172:         raise ValueError(f"greedy expansion failed for {system.name}")
  173:     return tuple(reversed(digits_msd))
  174:

  176: def is_canonical(system: LinearSystem, word: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
  177:     if not word or word[-1] == 0:
  178:         return False
  179:     if system.name == "fibonacci":
  180:         return all(left + right <= 1 for left, right in zip(word, word[1:]))
  181:     return tuple(word) == greedy_word(system, value(system, word))

  184: def matrix_order(matrix: Matrix, modulus: int, limit: int = 2_000_000) -> int:
  185:     if modulus < 2:
  186:         raise ValueError("modulus must be at least 2")
  187:     if gcd(determinant(matrix), modulus) != 1:
  188:         raise NonInvertibleAction(
  189:             f"determinant {determinant(matrix)} is not a unit modulo {modulus}"
  190:         )
  191:     reduced = tuple(tuple(entry % modulus for entry in row) for row in matrix)
  192:     target = identity(len(matrix))
  193:     power = target
  194:     for exponent in range(1, limit + 1):
  195:         power = matmul(reduced, power, modulus)
  196:         if power == target:
  197:             return exponent
  198:     raise RuntimeError(f"matrix order exceeded search limit {limit}")

  201: def pumped_word(word: Word, cuts: tuple[int, int, int, int], exponent: int) -> Word:
  202:     a, b, c, d = cuts
  203:     if not 0 <= a <= b <= c <= d <= len(word):
  204:         raise ValueError("cuts must be ordered positions in the word")
  205:     u, v, x, y, z = word[:a], word[a:b], word[b:c], word[c:d], word[d:]
  206:     if not v and not y:
  207:         raise ValueError("at least one pumped block must be nonempty")
  208:     return u + v * exponent + x + y * exponent + z
  209:

  211: def pump_disjoint_blocks(
  212:     word: Word, spans: Sequence[tuple[int, int]], exponent: int
  213: ) -> Word:
  214:     if exponent < 0:
  215:         raise ValueError("the pumping exponent must be nonnegative")
  216:     previous = 0
  217:     pieces: list[int] = []
  218:     nonempty = False
  219:     for start, stop in spans:
  220:         if not previous <= start <= stop <= len(word):
  221:             raise ValueError("pumped spans must be ordered and disjoint")
  222:         pieces.extend(word[previous:start])
  223:         block = word[start:stop]
  224:         pieces.extend(block * exponent)
  225:         nonempty = nonempty or bool(block)
  226:         previous = stop
  227:     if not nonempty:
  228:         raise ValueError("at least one pumped block must be nonempty")
  229:     pieces.extend(word[previous:])
  230:     return tuple(pieces)

  233: def tail_action_state(
  234:     recurrence: Sequence[int],
  235:     weight_values: Sequence[int],
  236:     prefix: Word,
  237:     suffix: Word,
  238: ) -> tuple[int, ...]:
  239:     """Apply suffix matrices to the state seeded after a fixed prefix."""
  240:     dimension = len(recurrence)
  241:     start = len(prefix)
  242:     required = start + len(suffix) + dimension
  243:     if dimension < 1 or len(weight_values) < required:
  244:         raise ValueError("insufficient recurrence or weight data for the suffix")
  245:     for index in range(start, len(weight_values) - dimension):
  246:         expected = sum(
  247:             recurrence[offset] * weight_values[index + offset]
  248:             for offset in range(dimension)
  249:         )
  250:         if weight_values[index + dimension] != expected:
  251:             raise ValueError("the supplied recurrence is not valid after the prefix")
  252: 
  253:     max_digit = max(prefix + suffix, default=0)
  254:     tail_system = LinearSystem(
  255:         name="tail_action",
  256:         polynomial="",
  257:         recurrence=tuple(recurrence),
  258:         initials=tuple(weight_values[start : start + dimension]),
  259:         max_digit=max_digit,
  260:     )
  261:     prefix_value = sum(
  262:         digit * weight for digit, weight in zip(prefix, weight_values)
  263:     )
  264:     seed = (prefix_value,) + tuple(weight_values[start : start + dimension])
  265:     return matvec(block_matrix(tail_system, suffix), seed)

  268: def linear_mcfg_ray_word(
  269:     prefix: Word,
  270:     constants: Sequence[Word],
  271:     left_pumps: Sequence[Word],
  272:     middles: Sequence[Word],
  273:     right_pumps: Sequence[Word],
  274:     exponent: int,
  275: ) -> Word:
  276:     """Evaluate the word produced after ``exponent`` ray recursions."""
  277:     if exponent < 0:
  278:         raise ValueError("the ray exponent must be nonnegative")
  279:     fan_out = len(left_pumps)
  280:     if not (
  281:         len(constants) == fan_out + 1
  282:         and len(middles) == fan_out
  283:         and len(right_pumps) == fan_out
  284:     ):
  285:         raise ValueError("inconsistent synchronized-ray block counts")
  286:     if not any(left_pumps) and not any(right_pumps):
  287:         raise ValueError("at least one synchronized pump must be nonempty")
  288: 
  289:     word = list(prefix)
  290:     for index in range(fan_out):
  291:         word.extend(constants[index])
  292:         word.extend(left_pumps[index] * exponent)
  293:         word.extend(middles[index])
  294:         word.extend(right_pumps[index] * exponent)
  295:     word.extend(constants[-1])
  296:     return tuple(word)

  299: def check_synchronized_orbit(
  300:     system: LinearSystem,
  301:     word: Word,
  302:     spans: Sequence[tuple[int, int]],
  303:     moduli: Iterable[int],
  304:     parameters: Iterable[int],
  305: ) -> int:
  306:     blocks = tuple(word[start:stop] for start, stop in spans if start < stop)
  307:     if not blocks:
  308:         raise ValueError("at least one pumped block must be nonempty")
  309:     tested = 0
  310:     parameter_values = tuple(parameters)
  311:     for modulus in moduli:
  312:         orders = tuple(
  313:             matrix_order(block_matrix(system, block), modulus) for block in blocks
  314:         )
  315:         return_time = lcm(*orders)
  316:         for parameter in parameter_values:
  317:             current = value(system, pump_disjoint_blocks(word, spans, parameter))
  318:             returned = value(
  319:                 system,
  320:                 pump_disjoint_blocks(word, spans, parameter + return_time),
  321:             )
  322:             if returned % modulus != current % modulus:
  323:                 raise AssertionError(
  324:                     f"synchronized congruence failed for {system.name}, "
  325:                     f"q={modulus}, t={parameter}"
  326:                 )
  327:             tested += 1
  328:     return tested

  331: def is_prime(number: int) -> bool:
  332:     if number < 2:
  333:         return False
  334:     if number % 2 == 0:
  335:         return number == 2
  336:     divisor = 3
  337:     while divisor * divisor <= number:
  338:         if number % divisor == 0:
  339:             return False
  340:         divisor += 2
  341:     return True
  342: 
  343: 
  344: def prime_factors(number: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
  345:     if number < 1:
  346:         raise ValueError("prime factorization is defined here only for positive integers")
  347:     factors = []
  348:     candidate = 2
  349:     remaining = number
  350:     while candidate * candidate <= remaining:
  351:         if remaining % candidate == 0:
  352:             factors.append(candidate)
  353:             while remaining % candidate == 0:
  354:                 remaining //= candidate
  355:         candidate = 3 if candidate == 2 else candidate + 2
  356:     if remaining > 1:
  357:         factors.append(remaining)
  358:     return tuple(factors)
  359: 
  360: 
  361: def valuation(number: int, prime: int) -> int:
  362:     exponent = 0
  363:     while number % prime == 0:
  364:         number //= prime
  365:         exponent += 1
  366:     return exponent
  367:

  369: def omega_outside(number: int, excluded_primes: Iterable[int]) -> int:
  370:     excluded = set(excluded_primes)
  371:     return sum(prime not in excluded for prime in prime_factors(number))

  431: def construct_deep_congruence_chain(
  432:     initial: int, specifications: Sequence[tuple[int, int]]
  433: ) -> tuple[int, ...]:

  438:         if modulus_factor < 1 or depth < 1:

  446: def construct_divisibility_tree(
  447:     root: int,
  448:     nodes: Sequence[tuple[int, ...]],
  449:     thresholds: dict[tuple[int, ...], int],
  450: ) -> tuple[dict[tuple[int, ...], int], dict[tuple[int, ...], int]]:
  451:     if not nodes or nodes[0] != () or root < 1:
  452:         raise ValueError("nodes must begin with the root and the root value must be positive")
  453:     values = {(): root}
  454:     edge_quotients: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
  455:     for node in nodes[1:]:
  456:         parent = node[:-1]
  457:         if parent not in values:
  458:             raise ValueError("every parent must precede its children")

  460:         small_prime_product = 1
  461:         for candidate in range(2, threshold + 1):
  462:             if is_prime(candidate):
  463:                 small_prime_product *= candidate

  465:         for quotient in edge_quotients.values():

  468:         quotient = 1 + parent_value * previous_product

  470:         edge_quotients[node] = quotient

  477:     cuts: tuple[int, int, int, int],
  478:     require_canonical: bool = False,
  479: ) -> PumpWitness:
  480:     original = value(system, word)
  481:     if not is_prime(original):
  482:         raise ValueError("the original word must represent a prime")
  483:     if original and system.trailing_coefficient % original == 0:
  484:         raise NonInvertibleAction("the represented prime divides the trailing coefficient")
  485:     a, b, c, d = cuts
  486:     v, y = word[a:b], word[c:d]
  487:     orders = [
  488:         matrix_order(block_matrix(system, block), original * original)
  489:         for block in (v, y)
  490:         if block
  491:     ]
  492:     return_time = lcm(*orders)
  493:     exponent = 1 + return_time
  494:     result_word = pumped_word(word, cuts, exponent)
  495:     result_value = value(system, result_word)
  496:     before = is_canonical(system, word)
  497:     after = is_canonical(system, result_word)
  498:     if require_canonical and not (before and after):
  499:         raise AssertionError("the selected pumping does not preserve canonical syntax")
  500:     if result_value % (original * original) != original:
  501:         raise AssertionError("square-modulus pumping congruence failed")
  502:     return PumpWitness(
  503:         system=system.name,
  504:         original_word="".join(map(str, word)),
  505:         original_value=original,
  506:         cuts=cuts,
  507:         return_time=return_time,
  508:         pump_exponent=exponent,
  509:         pumped_length=len(result_word),
  510:         pumped_value=result_value,
  511:         quotient_mod_original=(result_value // original) % original,
  512:         canonical_before=before,
  513:         canonical_after=after,
  514:     )
  515: 
  516: 
  517: def check_affine_action(system: LinearSystem, max_length: int = 5) -> int:
  518:     cases = 0
  519:     initial_state = (0,) + system.initials
  520:     for length in range(max_length + 1):
  521:         for word in product(range(system.max_digit + 1), repeat=length):
  522:             transformed = matvec(block_matrix(system, word), initial_state)
  523:             expected_weights = weights(system, length + system.dimension)[length:]
  524:             expected = (value(system, word),) + tuple(expected_weights)
  525:             if transformed != expected:
  526:                 raise AssertionError(
  527:                     f"affine action mismatch for {system.name}, word={word}: "
  528:                     f"{transformed} != {expected}"
  529:                 )
  530:             cases += 1
  531:     return cases
  532: 
  533: 
  534: def search_singular_counterexample() -> dict[str, int | str | bool]:
  535:     system = system_by_name("quadratic_nonunit")
  536:     matrix = block_matrix(system, (0,))
  537:     modulus = 2
  538:     return {
  539:         "system": system.name,
  540:         "polynomial": system.polynomial,
  541:         "modulus": modulus,
  542:         "trailing_coefficient": system.trailing_coefficient,
  543:         "block": "0",
  544:         "determinant": determinant(matrix),
  545:         "invertible": gcd(determinant(matrix), modulus) == 1,
  546:     }

  548: 
  549: def verify_inflated_fibonacci_separation(
  550:     primes: Sequence[int] = (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13),
  551:     maximum_power: int = 4,
  552:     maximum_index: int = 24,
  553: ) -> dict[str, int]:
  554:     """Check the ambient/reachable determinant separation for Fibonacci tails."""
  555:     fibonacci = [1, 2]
  556:     while len(fibonacci) <= maximum_index + 3:
  557:         fibonacci.append(fibonacci[-1] + fibonacci[-2])
  558: 
  559:     reachable_state = (1, 2, 3)
  560:     reachable_next = (2, 3, 5)
  561:     reachable_action = ((0, 1), (1, 1))
  562:     reachable_determinant = determinant(reachable_action)
  563:     saturation_minors = (
  564:         reachable_state[0] * reachable_next[1]
  565:         - reachable_state[1] * reachable_next[0],
  566:         reachable_state[0] * reachable_next[2]
  567:         - reachable_state[2] * reachable_next[0],
  568:         reachable_state[1] * reachable_next[2]
  569:         - reachable_state[2] * reachable_next[1],
  570:     )
  571: 
  572:     cases = 0
  573:     failures = 0
  574: 
  575:     def check(condition: bool) -> None:
  576:         nonlocal cases, failures
  577:         cases += 1
  578:         failures += int(not condition)
  579: 
  580:     check(gcd(*saturation_minors) == 1)
  581:     check(reachable_determinant == -1)
  582: 
  583:     for prime in primes:
  584:         inflated = LinearSystem(
  585:             name=f"inflated_fibonacci_{prime}",
  586:             polynomial=f"(x-{prime})(x^2-x-1)",
  587:             recurrence=(-prime, 1 - prime, prime + 1),
  588:             initials=reachable_state,
  589:             max_digit=1,
  590:         )
  591:         companion = tuple(
  592:             tuple(row[1:]) for row in digit_matrix(inflated, 0)[1:]
  593:         )
  594:         check(determinant(companion) == -prime)
  595:         check(matvec(companion, reachable_state) == reachable_next)
  596:         twice = matvec(companion, reachable_next)
  597:         check(
  598:             tuple(
  599:                 twice[index] - reachable_next[index] - reachable_state[index]
  600:                 for index in range(3)
  601:             )
  602:             == (0, 0, 0)
  603:         )
  604: 
  605:         for index in range(maximum_index + 1):
  606:             check(
  607:                 fibonacci[index + 3]
  608:                 == -prime * fibonacci[index]
  609:                 + (1 - prime) * fibonacci[index + 1]
  610:                 + (prime + 1) * fibonacci[index + 2]
  611:             )
  612: 
  613:         for power in range(1, maximum_power + 1):
  614:             modulus = prime**power
  615:             check(gcd(determinant(companion), modulus) != 1)
  616:             check(gcd(reachable_determinant, modulus) == 1)
  617:             state = tuple(entry % modulus for entry in reachable_state)
  618:             for _ in range(maximum_index + 1):
  619:                 following = tuple(entry % modulus for entry in matvec(companion, state))
  620:                 twice = tuple(entry % modulus for entry in matvec(companion, following))
  621:                 check(
  622:                     all(
  623:                         (twice[index] - following[index] - state[index]) % modulus
  624:                         == 0
  625:                         for index in range(3)
  626:                     )
  627:                 )
  628:                 check(any(entry % modulus for entry in state))
  629:                 state = following
  630: 
  631:     return {
  632:         "cases": cases,
  633:         "failures": failures,
  634:         "reachable_rank": 2,
  635:         "reachable_determinant": reachable_determinant,
  636:     }
  637: 
  638: 
  639: def run_verification() -> dict[str, object]:
  640:     affine_cases = sum(check_affine_action(system) for system in SYSTEMS)
  641:     examples = (
  642:         ("fibonacci", (0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), (2, 3, 4, 5)),
  643:         ("pell", (1, 0, 0, 1), (1, 2, 2, 3)),
  644:         ("tribonacci", (0, 0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 1, 2)),
  645:         ("quadratic_nonunit", (1, 0, 0, 1), (1, 2, 2, 3)),
  646:         ("integer_base_2", (1, 0, 0, 0, 1), (1, 2, 2, 3)),
  647:     )
  648:     witnesses = []
  649:     failures = 0
  650:     for name, word, cuts in examples:
  651:         try:
  652:             witnesses.append(
  653:                 asdict(
  654:                     verify_pump_witness(
  655:                         system_by_name(name), word, cuts, require_canonical=True
  656:                     )
  657:                 )
  658:             )
  659:         except AssertionError:
  660:             failures += 1
  661: 
  662:     synchronized_orbit_cases = check_synchronized_orbit(
  663:         system_by_name("fibonacci"),
  664:         (0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1),
  665:         ((2, 3), (4, 5)),
  666:         moduli=range(2, 21),
  667:         parameters=range(6),
  668:     )
  669:     synchronized_orbit_cases += check_synchronized_orbit(
  670:         system_by_name("quadratic_nonunit"),
  671:         (1, 0, 0, 1),
  672:         ((1, 2), (2, 3)),
  673:         moduli=range(3, 20, 2),
  674:         parameters=range(5),
  675:     )
  676: 
  677:     layer_point = 2 * 3 * 5**2 * 7
  678:     excluded_primes = (2, 3)
  679:     valuation_bounds = {2: 2, 3: 1}
  680:     isolation_modulus = local_layer_isolation_modulus(
  681:         layer_point, excluded_primes, valuation_bounds
  682:     )
  683:     layer_matches = [
  684:         number
  685:         for number in range(1, 50_001)
  686:         if in_local_prime_layer(number, 2, excluded_primes, valuation_bounds)
  687:         and (number - layer_point) % isolation_modulus == 0
  688:     ]
  689:     local_layer_isolation_failures = int(layer_matches != [layer_point])
  690: 
  691:     specifications = ((6, 1), (30, 2), (210, 1))
  692:     chain = construct_deep_congruence_chain(2, specifications)
  693:     deep_chain_failures = sum(
  694:         following % current != 0
  695:         or (following // current) % (modulus_factor * current**depth) != 1
  696:         for current, following, (modulus_factor, depth) in zip(
  697:             chain, chain[1:], specifications
  698:         )
  699:     )
  700: 
  701:     tree_nodes = ((), (0,), (1,), (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0))
  702:     thresholds = {(0,): 3, (1,): 5, (0, 0): 7, (0, 1): 11, (1, 0): 13}
  703:     tree_values, tree_edges = construct_divisibility_tree(2, tree_nodes, thresholds)
  704:     divisibility_tree_failures = sum(
  705:         (tree_values[right] % tree_values[left] == 0)
  706:         != (right[: len(left)] == left)
  707:         for left in tree_nodes
  708:         for right in tree_nodes
  709:     )
  710:     edge_values = tuple(tree_edges.values())
  711:     divisibility_tree_failures += sum(
  712:         gcd(left, right) != 1
  713:         for index, left in enumerate(edge_values)
  714:         for right in edge_values[index + 1 :]
  715:     )
  716:     divisibility_tree_failures += sum(
  717:         quotient % prime == 0
  718:         for edge, quotient in tree_edges.items()
  719:         for prime in range(2, thresholds[edge] + 1)
  720:         if is_prime(prime)
  721:     )
  722:     inflated_fibonacci = verify_inflated_fibonacci_separation()
  723: 
  724:     transient_weights = (1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 192)
  725:     transient_prefix = (2,)
  726:     tail_prefix_cases = 0
  727:     tail_prefix_failures = 0
  728:     for suffix_length in range(6):
  729:         for suffix in product((0, 1), repeat=suffix_length):
  730:             transformed = tail_action_state(
  731:                 (-10, 7), transient_weights, transient_prefix, suffix
  732:             )
  733:             full_word = transient_prefix + suffix
  734:             expected = (
  735:                 sum(
  736:                     digit * weight
  737:                     for digit, weight in zip(full_word, transient_weights)
  738:                 ),
  739:                 *transient_weights[
  740:                     len(full_word) : len(full_word) + 2
  741:                 ],
  742:             )
  743:             tail_prefix_cases += 1
  744:             tail_prefix_failures += int(transformed != expected)
  745: 
  746:     base_two = system_by_name("integer_base_2")
  747:     geometric_ray_cases = 13
  748:     geometric_ray_failures = sum(
  749:         value(
  750:             base_two,
  751:             linear_mcfg_ray_word(
  752:                 prefix=(),
  753:                 constants=((), (1,)),
  754:                 left_pumps=((0,),),
  755:                 middles=((),),
  756:                 right_pumps=((),),
  757:                 exponent=exponent,
  758:             ),
  759:         )
  760:         != 2**exponent
  761:         for exponent in range(geometric_ray_cases)
  762:     )
  763:     return {
  764:         "systems_checked": len(SYSTEMS),
  765:         "affine_cases": affine_cases,
  766:         "pump_witnesses": len(witnesses),
  767:         "congruence_failures": failures,
  768:         "synchronized_orbit_cases": synchronized_orbit_cases,
  769:         "local_layer_isolation_failures": local_layer_isolation_failures,
  770:         "deep_chain_failures": deep_chain_failures,
  771:         "divisibility_tree_failures": divisibility_tree_failures,
  772:         "inflated_fibonacci_cases": inflated_fibonacci["cases"],
  773:         "inflated_fibonacci_failures": inflated_fibonacci["failures"],
  774:         "tail_prefix_cases": tail_prefix_cases,
  775:         "tail_prefix_failures": tail_prefix_failures,
  776:         "geometric_ray_cases": geometric_ray_cases,
  777:         "geometric_ray_failures": geometric_ray_failures,
  778:         "witnesses": witnesses,
  779:         "counterexample": search_singular_counterexample(),
  780:     }

codex
1. **HEADLINE RESULT.** **Theorem 3.14 (`thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray`):** A canonical eventually recurrent numeration system contains an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL whose values have bounded prime support outside the constant-term primes of the minimal tail recurrence if and only if its canonical language contains a synchronized linear-MCFL ray \(W(t)\) with \(\operatorname{val}_U(W(t))=cb^t\) for integers \(c\ge1\), \(b\ge2\).

2. **IS IT ACTUALLY NEW? GENUINELY NEW.** The nearest prior results are Hartmanis–Shank, *On the Recognition of Primes by Automata* (1968), and Schützenberger, *A Remark on Acceptable Sets of Numbers* (1968), which establish fixed-base context-free prime immunity but give neither MCFL nor recurrent-numeration results. Seki–Matsumura–Fujii–Kasami (1991) supply the weak MCFL pumping orbit and Evertse, *On sums of \(S\)-units and linear recurrences* (1984), supplies the recurrence rigidity, but independent arXiv/OpenAlex/Crossref searches found no prior work combining them into this equivalence.

3. **DEPTH OF THE MATHEMATICS.** Moderate, not deep: the synchronized affine-congruence orbit is a real mechanism, but the difficult inputs are imported and the central proof becomes a short synthesis of weak pumping, finite-group periodicity, and Evertse’s theorem. The verification scripts are finite sanity checks, not evidence for the Diophantine or language-theoretic steps.

4. **TOP-JOURNAL VERDICT. TIER-3.** The new MCFL/Pisot theorem package is suitable for a solid specialist journal, but the proof depth and conceptual reach are below TIER-2, and much of the manuscript is classical density material or downstream corollaries.

5. **WHAT WOULD MOVE IT UP ONE TIER.** Prove a terminating decision algorithm for every effectively presented regular canonical linear Pisot \(U\)-system that decides whether \(\mathcal R_U\) contains a synchronized ray \(W(t)\) with \(\operatorname{val}_U(W(t))=cb^t\), equivalently whether it contains an infinite MCFL with bounded prime support; the present paper proves only positive semidecidability.

6. **WEAKEST LINK.** Lemma 3.13 (`lem:s-unit-increasing-recurrence-rigidity`): the reduction from an arbitrary integer recurrence with fixed prime support to an exact geometric arithmetic subsequence is compressed, and a referee will demand a complete verification of the nondegenerate decomposition, zero-root/cancellation cases, rationality of the surviving characteristic root, and the precise hypotheses of Evertse’s Theorem 3.
